summary: The article provides a largely accurate and helpful guide for salaried taxpayers on ITR filing, with most factual claims verified against authoritative sources. However, there are a few discrepancies regarding specific deduction limits and retention periods that should be reviewed.

claims.claim: Form 16 is issued by your employer and is a certificate stating the income paid to you and the Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on that income. You typically receive this by June 15th after the financial year ends.
claims.note: Employers are required to issue Form 16 by June 15th of the assessment year for the preceding financial year.

claims.claim: Section 80C allows deductions up to ₹1.5 lakhs for investments like Public Provident Fund (PPF), Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS), life insurance premiums, home loan principal repayment, and children's tuition fees.
claims.note: Section 80C allows a maximum deduction of ₹1.5 lakh for specified investments and expenses.

claims.claim: Section 80D offers deductions for health insurance premiums, while Section 80E covers interest on education loans.
claims.note: Section 80D provides deductions for health insurance premiums. Section 80E covers interest on education loans.
The standard deduction for salaried employees under the old tax regime is ₹50,000.

claims.claim: For those with home loans, ensure you have the interest certificate from your lender. For LTA, keep travel tickets and boarding passes as proof.
claims.note: An interest certificate from the lender is required to claim deductions on home loan interest under Section 24(b).

claims.claim: Standard Deduction: -₹50,000 (available in new regime from FY 2023-24 onwards for salaried individuals)
claims.note: The standard deduction of ₹50,000 for salaried individuals and pensioners is available under the new tax regime from FY 2023-24 onwards.

claims.claim: It is generally recommended to retain tax-related documents for at least 7-8 assessment years from the end of the relevant assessment year. This is because the Income Tax Department can reopen assessments for up to 7 years in certain cases.
claims.note: The Income Tax Department can generally reopen assessments for up to 6 years from the end of the relevant assessment year. For cases involving income of ₹50 lakh or more that has escaped assessment, the time limit is 10 years. For foreign assets or income, it can extend to 16 years. It is generally recommended to keep documents for at least 8 years.

claims.claim: Yes, if your gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, filing an ITR is mandatory, even if all your tax has been deducted at source.
claims.note: Filing an ITR is mandatory if gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, even if TDS has been deducted. It is also mandatory if TDS/TCS exceeds ₹25,000 (₹50,000 for senior citizens).

article_title: Your ITR Filing Checklist: A Month-Wise Guide for Salaried Taxpayers
